findings.what: I-084, pawanmali's 'successor-skip' division addition (pawanmali/biohub-942tta-fork-succskip-v1, cell 10.5). THE IDEA: x138's safe-division stage uses the same add_safe_divisions_postlink code (exp70g.py l.4087+). It rejects a candidate outright when the existing child c1 or the candidate q lacks a UNIQUE successor at t+2, because divergence cannot be checked. succskip waives only that missing-data case and keeps every other gate (parent 9, sister 14, mutual NN, DC >= 0.25, tau 0.6, caps). The author's own pipeline gave +0.0017 (TP 7->8, FP 24->27), which is one event. OLD VERDICT (16 Sep code scan): closed by CLASS and never measured: 'post-processing class closed on LB; not probed' (CONTEXT l.987-992; IDEAS I-084). WHAT CHANGED: the class premise is false. Division-side knobs do move the public board: probe 41 (dc0.30) -0.005, probe 45 (cap 6) +0.002 through ADDs. A division ADD on the DC-gated path is exactly the kind of lever the public board rewards. MEASURED TODAY (exp60 x138 lab, 56 clips; K2-like bed and exp70g-like cap-6 insertion bed; scratch r21_ssk.py): (1) DC-unfiltered upper bound: +464 forks on 676 (+69%) and +499 nodes. The nodes come from KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS keeping the rescued 1-frame fragments. Added forks: 0 TP / 4 FP / 478 ignored. Score: K2-like bed -0.00048 (6bba -0.00060, 44b6 -0.00003); cap-6 bed -0.00062 (6bba -0.00076). Per-clip W/L 1/43. (2) Split by case: '01' (c1 ends, q continues; this is the author's final-graph case) adds +265 forks, 0 TP / 3 FP. '10' (q is a 1-frame blip) adds +152 forks, 0 TP / 2 FP. No count-2 case ever reaches the check. (3) The kernel never DC-scored the rescued points, so the lab cannot apply the DC veto. Lower bound (only rescues with a recorded DC score): +7 forks, all ignored. At the measured DC pass rate of 25-28% of geometric candidates (44b6 683/2736, 6bba 1080/3881), the kernel would add about +120 forks (+18%). That is the same volume as tau 0.75, which on the same bed added 6 TP / 5 FP on 6bba, against 0 TP / 4 FP here. NEW VERDICT: UPHELD, now on a measured reason instead of a class reason. The rescued set is TP-empty in the lab and inflates the node count. As a geometric ADD it is dominated by tau 0.75. It is new code, so it has no path through R8 or the W1/W2/W4 v3 tables.

findings.what: Lab calibration. In the exp60 replay (tools/trainlab.py DCLookup, l.256-269), a point the kernel never DC-scored returns None and is ACCEPTED. In add_safe_divisions_postlink the gate order is: parent <= 9 -> sister <= 14 -> mutual NN -> divergence -> DeepCenter >= 0.25 -> tau. So any arm that RELAXES a gate placed before the DC check replays without the DC veto on its extra forks: parent radius, sister radius, no-MNN, looser divergence, succskip. For those arms: (a) the added volume is overstated about 3.5-4x, since DC passes only 25% (44b6) / 28% (6bba) of geometric candidates; (b) the added-fork precision comes from a DC-unfiltered pool. Affected numbers: round 13 R13DP-1 par10 / sis16 / nomnn / div1.75 (div1.75: +620 forks, 0 TP / +12 FP), and today's par10 / par11 / succskip arms (dc_miss 1,175 / 2,362 / all rescues). Arms that tighten a gate, or relax one placed AFTER DC (tau, the DC threshold itself), replay exactly; this is why round 19's tau numbers are exact.
